note: Etihad Credit Bureau's own FAQs (etihadbureau.ae/faqs, read 2026-10-30; the answers are in the page's data, the personal ones tagged PERSONAL): for individuals, defaults, missed payments and bounced cheques always appear in the credit report up to five years, even after the payment is settled (written as keep five years); the report's month-by-month payment history covers the last 36 months and each facility shows a 24-month colour-coded history (a delay up to 90 days yellow, over 90 days red). The bureau collects under Federal Credit Information Law 6 of 2010 as amended by Federal Decree-Law 8 of 2020, whose texts (uaelegislation.gov.ae, Cloudflare; the bureau's translations, now 404) weren't read. The business FAQ says three years for companies' marks; the file is for a person, so it uses the personal answer. Information providers submit updated data daily (the non-banking sector monthly), with no threshold stated: written as reported one day after the due date (as Yemen's daily submission is), the bank's card being a bank's credit.

sources.title: Etihad Credit Bureau: FAQs (personal credit report and general)
sources.said: Defaults missed payments and bounced cheques will always appear in your Credit Report up to a period of 5 years. ... Information providers submit updated data to Etihad Credit Bureau on daily basis. For non-banking sector, data is submitted on a monthly basis due to its less dynamic nature. ... If the payment for a particular month was paid with a delay up to 90 days after the due date, the box will be shaded yellow.
